verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The warming phase of the sea surface temperature is known as "El Niño" and the cooling phase as "La Niña"."

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The warming phase of the sea surface temperature is known as "El Niño" and the cooling phase as "La Niña"."

verifications.claim: According to Wikipedia, El Niño and La Niña are opposing, natural climate patterns in the tropical Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a global climate phenomenon that emerges from variation in winds and sea surface temperatures over the tropical Pacific Ocean." "La Niña and El Niño are opposite phases in the oscillation"
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia (R7) describes them as opposite phases of a natural climate phenomenon in the tropical Pacific.

verifications.claim: According to Wikipedia, El Niño and La Niña are known as the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The El Niño–Southern Oscillation is a single climate phenomenon that periodically fluctuates between three phases: Neutral, La Niña or El Niño."
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia (R7) defines ENSO as the phenomenon encompassing El Niño and La Niña phases.

verifications.claim: El Niño and La Niña affect global weather every 2–7 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "the cycle alternating every three to seven years"; R2: "interval has varied from 2 to 7 years"; R6: "El Niño and La Niña events occur every two to seven years"; R7: "typically occur every two to seven years"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the 2-7 year cycle affecting global weather.

verifications.claim: A 2026 forecast shows El Niño potentially bringing warmer, drier conditions to the northern U.S.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: "the North stays relatively dry and warm on average"; R4: "warmer-than-normal temperatures to the northern United States"
verifications.reasoning: 2026 El Niño forecasts in R3 and R4 explicitly predict warmer and drier conditions in northern U.S.

verifications.claim: A 2026 forecast shows La Niña bringing wetter, cooler conditions to the northern U.S.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "2025–26 winter" La Niña forecast with "cooler temperatures more likely in parts of the northern Plains and Pacific Northwest" and "wetter conditions in portions of the North"; R2: "La Niña episodes feature ... colder and stormier than average conditions across the North"
verifications.reasoning: R1 provides a 2025-26 (overlapping 2026) La Niña forecast matching wetter/cooler northern U.S.; R2 supports general La Niña impacts. Specific 2026 La Niña forecast is slightly vague but aligns.
